justification: The implementation of the Farm to Fork Strategy can reinforce the European Climate Law by promoting sustainable agriculture practices, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and enhancing biodiversity, which are all crucial for achieving climate neutrality.

The Farm to Fork Strategy can enable the implementation of the urban wastewater treatment recast by promoting the use of treated wastewater for irrigation, reducing the environmental impact of agriculture, and increasing water efficiency.

The Farm to Fork Strategy may constrain the implementation of the Amending Directive 2003/87/EC by limiting the use of certain pesticides and fertilizers, which could impact agricultural productivity and the achievement of the directive's objectives.

The Farm to Fork Strategy can reinforce the Amending Regulation (EU) 2018/842 by promoting sustainable land use, reducing deforestation, and enhancing ecosystem services, which are all essential for achieving the regulation's objectives.

The Farm to Fork Strategy may counteract the Amending Regulations (EU) 2018/841 by promoting sustainable agriculture practices that could limit the use of certain land-use practices, which could impact the achievement of the regulation's objectives.

impact_policydoc: On an EU Strategy to reduce methane emissions
justification: The implementation of the Farm to Fork Strategy can be indivisible from the EU Strategy to reduce methane emissions, as it promotes sustainable agriculture practices, reduces enteric fermentation, and enhances manure management, which are all crucial for reducing methane emissions.

The Farm to Fork Strategy may limit the implementation of the A Renovation Wave for Europe by promoting energy-efficient buildings and reducing energy consumption, which could impact the achievement of the strategy's objectives.
